newsitem.title: BANGLADESH: Bangladesh floods kill four, make thousands homeless.
newsitem.headline: Bangladesh floods kill four, make thousands homeless.

text.p: At least four people have died and thousands made homeless in floods sweeping souheastern Bangladesh, government officials said on Monday.
The deluge began on Thursday as residents were still recovering from last month's floods which killed at least 100 people.
Officials said the latest flooding damaged thousands of houses, cut off roads, threatened train services and swamped crops on 50,000 acres (20,000 hectares) in Chittagong and Cox's Bazar districts.

Flood waters had started to subside since rain stopped on Sunday, they said. Road links between Cox's Bazar and the port of Chittagong and Teknaf along the Burmese border had been restored, they said.
But large areas in Cox's Bazar district still remained under three to four feet of water, with thousands of homes half submerged.
Many residents had moved to higher ground but were facing a shortage of dry food and clean water, officials in Cox's Bazar said on Monday.
The four deaths were reported from the worst-hit Ramu area, they said.
Officials were unable to estimate the cost of damage to crops and property. "This will be available only after the floods have fully receded," one said.
